clue.text: Suppress mischievous child — it's sent back

indicators.note: something sent back goes the way it came, so both pieces are read from right to left together

parts.note: an elf is a mischievous little creature, applied to an impish child
it's written without its apostrophe gives three letters

explanation.surface: A parent tries to quell a naughty child, who is being sent home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns the whole run ELF + ITS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother or hold something in check is to stifle it, as one stifles a yawn.

clue.text: Vehicle rounding curve gets a nasty shock

indicators.note: the vehicle goes round the curve, so it encloses the bend's letter

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle on rails
a U-bend is a curve shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: A tram taking a bend too fast gives its passengers a nasty fright.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotional wound from a sudden distressing event is a psychological shock.

clue.text: Unusually gifted journalist made to feel uneasy

indicators.note: done unusually, in an odd way, so the letters of the next word come out in a new order

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A remarkably talented reporter has been left feeling awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' looks like it qualifies 'gifted', but it rearranges GIFTED into FIDGET.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives a transitive sense of the verb, to make someone restless or uneasy.

clue.text: Secret circle I organised like this?

definitions.text: Secret circle I organised like this?

indicators.note: organised means put into a new arrangement, so the letters gathered here are reordered

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clandestine society, set up by the speaker, asks whether this is how it should be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges SECRET plus O and I; the whole clue is also the definition, a secret circle being obscure to outsiders.
explanation.definitionFit: Something understood only by an inner circle of initiates is arcane, as a secret society's lore would be.

clue.text: Attractive sort of field

definitions.meaning: charming in a way that draws people in, as a forceful personality does
the region around a magnet or current where its force acts is this kind of field

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from magnets: one literal, the field of force, one figurative, alluring charm.

clue.text: Source of certification received by vehicles left for examination

indicators.note: the vehicles take in the next piece, so it goes inside them

parts.note: media are vehicles or channels for communication

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so take its opening letter

explanation.surface: A doctor's note requires attending a vehicle check, with cars left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vehicles' suggests cars, but MEDIA (plural of medium) are vehicles of expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A health check-up by a doctor, as for insurance or employment, is a physical test.

clue.text: Supplied accounts worked over and assessed

indicators.note: over in a down clue turns the word above it upside down, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a machine that worked ran
assessed means rated, as a film is rated

explanation.surface: Someone gave reports after the figures were processed and evaluated.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell a story is to give an account of events, so a storyteller supplied accounts.

clue.text: One-way entrance to French town for visitors

indicators.note: the pieces make an entrance into the town, going inside it

parts.note: Tours is a city on the Loire in France
I is the Roman numeral for one
ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: Sightseers find the road into a French town is one-way only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-way' reads as a traffic sign on the road into town; the hyphen hides two separate pieces. Tours is a city on the Loire.
explanation.definitionFit: Holidaymakers sightseeing in a place are its visitors.

clue.text: Energy displayed in family groups keen for total victory

indicators.note: the energy is displayed inside the family groups, so its letter sits within them

parts.note: clans are family groups, as in Scotland
E is the physics symbol for energy
to keen is to wail in grief, to weep

explanation.surface: Enthusiastic families show great energy as they push for a decisive win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen' looks like an adjective, eager, but is the verb meaning to lament.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning every game or prize in a contest is a complete rout of the opposition.

clue.text: Crewman with Nelson, say, gets help when climbing rigging

parts.note: a hand is a member of a ship's crew
a nelson is a wrestling hold, so it is one example

explanation.surface: A sailor serving with Admiral Nelson gets help climbing the ship's ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nelson' points to the admiral, but here it is the wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A grip for the fingers lets a climber pull up, as on ropes or a rock face.

clue.text: Gamekeeper's opening ploy to trap old bird

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
the ploy traps the next piece, so it is caught inside

parts.note: a ruse is a crafty ploy

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper's first trick is a scheme to snare an elderly bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A plump game bird shot on moors in season is the classic gamekeeper's quarry.

clue.text: North American girl put in prison

indicators.note: the girl is put inside the prison, so her name sits within it

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
Nadia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman from across the Atlantic has been locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the country north of the United States is a North American.

clue.text: Cabaret turn one appears in is cause of ill-feeling

indicators.note: the numeral appears inside the rearranged word
a turn of the letters changes their order, rearranging the word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cabaret act with someone performing in it causes resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like a stage act but rearranges CABARET into BACTERA, with I inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Germs that cause infections make you feel ill, so they are a source of sickness.

clue.text: How one might impart confidence? It's overdue

definitions.meaning: a secret is whispered with a cupped palm shielding the mouth
late, in arrears with payments or work

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the gesture of whispering a confidence, the other an old word for late or in arrears.

clue.text: Was obliged to remove tails of fish

parts.note: had to do something means was obliged to
to dock an animal is to cut off its tail

explanation.surface: Someone was forced to cut the tails off some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A North Atlantic food fish related to cod, popular in fish and chips.

clue.text: Wife clothed in cheaper fashion in city centre

parts.note: prices that are down are cheaper

indicators.note: the wife is dressed in the fashion, so her letter goes inside

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style, as in bon ton

explanation.surface: A wife wears budget clothes when shopping in the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: TON for fashion is an old borrowing from French, still seen in bon ton.
explanation.definitionFit: The central business district of a city, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Impossible to move through road and tube chaos

indicators.note: chaos puts things in disorder, here the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Getting anywhere is impossible amid chaos on the roads and the Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn and unyielding, someone who will not be persuaded to change.

clue.text: Instant diets — spelling alterations for dressmaker

parts.note: a mo is an instant, as in half a mo

indicators.note: spelling here means signifying, so the word before calls for its letters altered

explanation.surface: Crash diets mean a seamstress must keep altering clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling alterations' means indicating rearrangement of DIETS into DISTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliner or maker of fashionable women's clothes, from the French.

clue.text: Men featured in 'ornblower's noted work

indicators.note: the men are featured within the next name, so they go inside it

parts.note: the fictional naval hero Horatio Hornblower, dropping the H as the apostrophe shows
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Sailors appear in a well-known episode of the Hornblower naval stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The missing H of 'ornblower' tells you to drop the H from his first name too, giving ORATIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A large musical composition for voices on a sacred theme, so a work set to notes.

clue.text: Maltreat four taken in as creating deception

indicators.note: four is taken in by the first verb, so its numeral goes inside

parts.note: to ill-use someone is to maltreat them
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: A quartet is badly treated after being duped by a con.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceptive and unreal, giving a false impression, like an illusion.

clue.text: Cover showing the passion that's in novel

indicators.note: the passion is inside the novel, so its letters go within that title

parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard
heat is passion, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: A book jacket reveals the steamy romance inside the novel.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE is H. Rider Haggard's adventure novel of 1887, about the immortal queen Ayesha.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a blade in a scabbard is to encase it, so the verb means to cover.

clue.text: Travelling light at the front

parts.note: read as packing little on the march at the front of a column, but meaning a lamp carried on the front of a vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: A car's main forward lamp lights the road while the vehicle travels.

clue.text: Precise moment

definitions.meaning: exact and detailed, as in a careful examination
a very short span of time, sixty seconds

explanation.definitionFit: Pronounced differently, one spelling means exact and tiny, the other sixty seconds.

clue.text: Condemn lair used by wild cat

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A hideout taken over by a big cat is declared unfit.
explanation.walkthrough: OUNCE looks like a weight but is the snow leopard of Central Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to publicly declare something wrong, to condemn it.

clue.text: You or I, perhaps, could be said to follow a solemn promise

indicators.note: this piece is said to follow, so it comes after the a
could be said means what follows is pronounced like another word

parts.note: the letters U and I are examples of vowels

explanation.surface: We could be said to make a serious pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You or I' looks like people but sounds the letters U and I, both vowels.
explanation.definitionFit: A declaration or affirmation, often made solemnly, as when someone swears.

clue.text: Times run arranged for end of training

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, here the letters of the two words before

explanation.surface: The newspaper organises a race to mark the end of a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' suggests coaching, but the definition is the end of a train line.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway station at the end of a line is where trains finish.

clue.text: Ballerina's singular entry into European employment

definitions.note: the 's means is, so the definition is just a ballerina

indicators.note: the singular makes its entry into the European, going inside

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
use is employment, as in putting to use

explanation.surface: A ballet dancer is the only European to have joined the company.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a female ballet dancer, a ballerina.

clue.text: Writer's inclusion in reference book cleared

indicators.note: the writer is included in the reference book, so goes inside it

parts.note: OED, the Oxford English Dictionary, is the classic reference book
a pen is a writer, used for writing

explanation.surface: An author's entry in an encyclopedia clears their name.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleared path or way is one that has been unblocked.
